candidate.title: How YOLOv8n Detects Objects, and How to Run yolo-s3-job

modules.title: Images and what an object detector produces

lessons.title: An image as numbers
topics: Pixel grid, colour channels, and image size
Why a model resizes an image to a fixed input size
Nothing in an image is labelled: meaning must be inferred

lessons.title: Labels, boxes, and confidence
topics: Classification (one label per image) versus detection (several located objects)
A detection = class label + rectangular box + confidence score
Confidence as the model's score for that prediction, not a probability of being correct

modules.title: Prerequisites: trained models and learned features

lessons.title: Weights, training, and inference
topics: Parameters (weights) fitted on labelled example images
Training versus inference: this app only runs inference
yolov8n.pt as a stored weights file; 'n' = nano, the smallest variant of the YOLOv8 family
A pretrained model recognises only the fixed class vocabulary it was trained on

lessons.title: Convolutional feature extraction
topics: Filters applied over small pixel neighbourhoods to produce feature maps
Downsampling: fewer, coarser spatial locations carrying richer descriptions
Layer stacking: edges and textures to parts to whole-object evidence

lessons.title: One pass, backbone and neck
topics: A single forward pass over the whole image rather than a sliding search
Backbone: extracting features at several resolutions
Neck: combining resolutions so small and large objects are both represented
Predictions attached to spatial locations in the feature grids

lessons.title: The anchor-free split detection head
topics: Split (decoupled) branches: class scores separate from box geometry
Anchor-free: box edges predicted directly at a location, without predefined anchor shapes
Why one real object generates many overlapping raw predictions

lessons.title: From raw predictions to a final list
topics: Score filtering: discarding predictions below a confidence value
Non-maximum suppression: keeping the highest-scoring box among overlapping duplicates for the same object
CPU inference: same computation as on a GPU, longer wall-clock time

lessons.title: Inputs and the confidence control
topics: S3 image path as input; optional output bucket as destination
Confidence threshold (default 0.5): sets the minimum score a prediction must reach to be reported
Raising it reports fewer, higher-scored detections; lowering it reports more, including weaker ones — it does not change what the model computed and does not by itself establish accuracy
A per-image job: one image in, one set of outputs

lessons.title: Reading annotated.jpg and boxes.json
topics: annotated.jpg: detections drawn as boxes on the image, so location is visible there
boxes.json: label and confidence pairs; box coordinates are not written into this file even though the model computes them to draw the annotation
Choosing which output to inspect for 'what' versus 'where'
Objects outside the model's class vocabulary, or scored below the threshold, appear in neither output

prerequisites: Comfort viewing image files and reading a simple text/JSON file
No machine learning, mathematics, or programming background assumed
An image location and any run access supplied by the app owner
scopeNotes: Training procedure (loss functions, label assignment, dataset construction) and model comparison are excluded; the goal is understanding inference and running this job.

App behaviour here comes from a supplied description, not from inspection of the deployed code or weights; the Ultralytics documentation describes the standard YOLOv8 family, not the specific deployed yolov8n.pt.
The exact class vocabulary of the deployed weights is not established by the supplied evidence; the course will state this as an unknown rather than name a dataset.

duration.explanation: Twenty minutes can cover Modules 1 and 4 plus a stated summary of YOLOv8's structure, but it cannot also build the beginner foundations (learned weights, convolutional features, anchor-free split head, NMS) that make the mechanism understandable. Keeping the stated conceptual goal requires a longer session; this is a planning judgement, not a measured learning time.

ownerQuestions: Extend beyond 20 minutes to keep Modules 2 and 3, or approve a 20-minute overview that describes YOLOv8's outputs and the threshold without explaining feature extraction and the detection head?
Should the course name the detectable classes? That requires confirming the training dataset of the deployed weights, which the supplied evidence does not cover.
